title: Top 10 Autonomous Medical Coding Software with CDI Capabilities
summary: Compare 10 autonomous medical coding platforms on how they handle CDI: alert vs. query logic, provider queries, explainability, and payer intelligence.
body_markdown:
> The best autonomous medical coding software doesn't treat CDI as a separate step — it evaluates documentation sufficiency while it codes, so missing specificity, unsupported diagnoses, and medical-necessity gaps are caught before billing, not weeks later in a denial queue.
>
>
> CombineHealth ranks first for exactly this: it's a[self-learning autonomous coding platform](https://www.combinehealth.ai/ai-medical-coding-software) with CDI built into the same coding pass, generating compliant provider queries, explaining every code with an audit trail, and learning from payer outcomes. In a 400-bed hospital deployment, that integrated approach surfaced **5× more CDI opportunities than the manual workflow while cutting coding-related denials 75%** .


A medical code can be correct and still get denied when the underlying documentation lacks specificity, fails to support a diagnosis, or does not establish medical necessity. If these gaps reach billing undetected, they can lead to denials, rework, and revenue loss.


Autonomous medical coding software can help identify these gaps during the medical coding stage itself. Clinical documentation improvement (CDI) plays a key role by flagging missing specificity, unsupported diagnoses, and medical-necessity gaps before claims are submitted, rather than weeks later in a denial queue.


This guide compares 10 autonomous medical coding platforms based on how they integrate coding with CDI and how that integration affects denial rates, audit trails, and coding team workloads.

## 1. CombineHealth


[CombineHealth](https://www.combinehealth.ai/) is a **self-learning autonomous medical coding platform with CDI integrated directly into the medical coding workflow.** It reads the complete clinical encounter, assigns or audits medical codes, identifies documentation gaps, applies coding guidance and payer-specific requirements, and provides an evidence trail behind every recommendation.


CombineHealth covers[ICD-10-CM](https://www.combinehealth.ai/) ,[CPT](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/cpt-codes-what-are-they-types-and-uses) , HCPCS Level II,[E/M levels](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/e-m-coding-guide) ,[modifiers](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/e-m-coding-guide) , and provider attribution across professional and facility settings.


### Why CombineHealth Ranks First


CombineHealth **** connects[clinical documentation improvement (CDI)](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/clinical-documentation-improvement-software) , autonomous coding, payer-aware claim validation, claim outcomes, and[payer intelligence](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/payer-intelligence-ai-medical-coding) in one workflow. **This helps identify problems that can lead to denials even when a medical code is technically correct.** These include missing documentation, unsupported medical necessity, payer-required modifiers or other claim conditions, incorrect diagnosis-to-procedure linkage, and unapplied provider-, facility-, or site-specific rules.


**Across deployments, CombineHealth has delivered:**


- **97.2%+ coding accuracy**
- **Up to 85% autonomous coding**
- **75% fewer coding-related denials**
- **4% higher captured revenue**
- **5× more CDI opportunities**
- **Sub-12-hour turnaround at volume**


### Feature #1: Integrated Coding and CDI in One Workflow


While coding, CombineHealth flags documentation issues that could affect a medical code or a claim, including:


- Missing specificity
- Contradictory documentation
- Unsupported diagnoses or procedures
- Missing critical-care time
- [E/M selection](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/e-m-coding-guide) gaps
- Medical-necessity issues
- Missed diagnoses or billable services
- Payer-specific documentation requirements


CombineHealth also distinguishes between when to send[CDI alerts and CDI queries](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/cdi-query-vs-alert) . CDI alerts track gaps for provider education; CDI queries require clarification before coding is finalized. Depending on the workflow, supported encounters are coded or charts held for provider review.


> **Recommended read:**[CDI Best Practices for Healthcare Organizations](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/cdi-best-practices-for-healthcare)


### Feature #2: Explainable Code-Level Rationale


Each ****[AI medical coding](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-medical-coding) and CDI decision includes the **documentation reviewed, relevant clinical evidence, selected code, applicable guidelines or payer requirements,** E/M medical decision-making, identified documentation gaps, review-routing reasons, and final decision with an[audit trail](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/ai-audit-trail-work-for-medical-coding) **.** Medical coders and auditors can review this evidence to support OIG reviews, payer audits, and internal compliance programs.


### Feature #3: Complete-Encounter Documentation Validation


CombineHealth’s autonomous medical coding platform reads the full clinical note, not just charge summaries or structured extracts, to validate each medical code. It **flags diagnosis-to-procedure linkage gaps** , insufficient specificity, and unsupported modifiers as CDI opportunities before claims reach billing.


### Feature #4: Self-Learning Payer Intelligence


After adjudication, CombineHealth analyzes denials, reimbursements, and underpayments to identify recurring payer patterns. **These patterns can inform proposed changes to future coding and claim-validation policies** after human validation. The platform does not automatically rewrite production coding policies after every denial.


> **CombineHealth Helped Brault Scale Their Autonomous Coding by 5x with 98% Accuracy**
>
>
> After a previous autonomous medical coding vendor failed to maintain production accuracy, Brault audited CombineHealth through parallel coding. **CombineHealth achieved 99.1% ICD, 98.4% CPT, 98.2% E/M, and 98.7% MIPS accuracy, with turnaround under 12 hours during 2-3× volume spikes.**[Read the Brault case study](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/brault-autonomous-coding)


**Best for:** Hospitals, health systems, physician groups, and RCM organizations that want coding and CDI working as one system.


## 2. Solventum 360 Encompass


Solventum 360 Encompass combines computer-assisted coding (CAC) with CDI 3D, which uses natural language processing (NLP) to identify documentation opportunities. The platform also offers an autonomous coding module, but only eligible encounters qualify for touchless processing. Other charts still require coder review through the standard CAC workflow.


Confirm which encounter types qualify for autonomous processing before evaluating the platform's automation capabilities.


**Key features:**


- Computer-assisted coding with autonomous processing for eligible encounters
- CDI 3D case-finding that analyzes documentation as it's entered
- Real-time clinical intelligence reporting across coding and CDI
- Cloud-based SaaS or on-premises deployment options


**Best for:** Hospitals already using Solventum or 3M tools that prioritize inpatient DRG accuracy and integrated CDI over fully autonomous coding.


## 3. AGS Health


AGS Health's AI Platform offers Autonomous medical coding, Computer-Assisted Coding, and Computer-Assisted CDI as separate modules connected through a shared data layer. Its CDI module includes query templates and intelligent worklists that prioritize charts based on potential impact.


The platform also tracks variance between CDI's coding assumptions and the codes that actually go out on claims, giving teams a direct way to measure alignment between the two functions.


**Key features:**


- Human-in-the-loop autonomous coding with expert coder review
- Computer-Assisted CDI with a built-in query template library
- Intelligent worklists that prioritize charts by impact
- Shared data platform across coding, HIM, and CDI


**Best for:** Hospitals wanting AI-assisted coding backed by certified coders and CDI specialists.


## 4. CorroHealth


CorroHealth combines PULSE coding automation with VISION, a separate clinical validation product for CDI, under its clinical revenue integrity offering. Generative AI reviews clinical records and flags documentation inconsistencies, while human CDI specialists write queries following AHIMA guidelines.


Its physician-led prospective CDI reviews cover inpatient and outpatient settings, helping providers address documentation gaps before charts reach the coding queue.


**Key features:**


- PULSE coding automation paired with VISION CDI validation
- AI-assisted query routing with human-written queries
- Charge capture and revenue integrity reviews
- Consulting to improve documentation practices upstream


**Best for:** Hospitals seeking coding, CDI, and revenue integrity services from one vendor while retaining specialist-written queries.


## 5. Nym


Nym's Clinical Language Understanding (CLU) engine converts provider notes directly into ICD-10-CM and CPT codes without human intervention on its primary medical coding path. Ambiguous charts are routed for review rather than coded through guesswork. Nym describes its engine as working alongside CDI programs to flag documentation gaps in real time.


The CLU engine also detects negation, historical references, and timing cues in clinical notes to support accurate diagnosis and procedure coding.


**Key features:**


- Autonomous coding with a complete audit trail
- Real-time documentation-gap detection alongside CDI programs
- SOC 2 Type II-certified platform
- Published, predictable implementation timeline


**Best for:** Health systems in Nym's supported specialties that already operate a CDI program.


## 6. Access Healthcare


Access Healthcare offers autonomous medical coding platforms alongside a separate, human-staffed CDI service. CDI specialists review documentation and contact physicians directly, rather than routing queries through an AI-native workflow. The company's materials position CDI as a staffing and process service distinct from its coding automation technology.


Its arc.in platform provides real-time visibility into coding and CDI productivity, helping leaders track throughput across both service lines through one dashboard.


**Key features:**


- Multiple autonomous coding platforms using OCR and HL7
- Human-staffed CDI services with global delivery support
- Separate coding and CDI service lines
- Flexible onsite or offsite CDI staffing


**Best for:** Organizations seeking outsourced coding capacity that are comfortable managing CDI as a separate service.


## 7. Fathom


Fathom provides touchless autonomous coding across ICD, CPT/HCPCS, E/M, modifiers, and provider assignment. It supports multiple specialties deployed simultaneously rather than requiring department-by-department rollouts.


Its documentation capabilities focus on flagging deficiencies rather than providing a named CDI query-management workflow.


**Key features:**


- Simultaneous multi-specialty autonomous coding
- Documentation-deficiency flagging alongside coding output
- Ongoing audit programs to validate coding accuracy
- Touchless coding across professional and facility settings


**Best for:** Health systems seeking enterprise-scale autonomous coding across multiple specialties.


## 8. CodaMetrix


CodaMetrix's CMX CARE platform analyzes the full longitudinal patient record, including problem lists, labs, imaging, and prior visits, rather than relying on a single encounter note. This context supports diagnostic specificity in complex, multi-visit cases such as sepsis and heart failure staging. Its public materials describe denial-data learning and coder review, but not a native CDI alert, query, or provider-response workflow.


Coded results flow directly into the charge router through HL7 and FHIR integrations, reducing handoffs between chart review and billing.


**Key features:**


- Contextual coding using the full longitudinal patient record
- Denial-data learning to improve performance over time
- Epic Toolbox designation for autonomous coding
- Specialty-specific models for radiology, pathology, and surgery


**Best for:** Large Epic health systems needing multi-specialty coding with deep clinical context.


## 9. RapidClaims


RapidClaims combines autonomous, assisted, and audit coding modes with its Intelligent CDI Suite, which includes query messaging, tracking, and analytics for documentation trends and query resolution. Its RapidRules engine tracks payer rule changes to help prevent denials proactively.


The platform's few-shot learning adapts to an organization's documentation style and historical charts rather than applying the same generic model to every client.


**Key features:**


- Autonomous, assisted, and audit coding modes in one platform
- Intelligent CDI Suite with query messaging and tracking
- RapidRules engine for proactive payer-rule monitoring
- Provider-level documentation analytics and training insights


**Best for:** Provider groups transitioning from assisted to autonomous coding that need a dedicated CDI workflow.


## 10. Optum Enterprise CAC and CDI 3D


Optum's Enterprise CAC and CDI 3D platform uses its Clinical Language Intelligence NLP engine to combine computer-assisted coding (CAC) with real-time documentation review. Optum describes the platform as computer-assisted rather than autonomous or touchless coding, with human CDI staff managing query responses through a mobile app.


Optum also offers an on-site CDI physician-champion program that combines automated case-finding with in-person provider education to improve documentation practices over time.


**Key features:**


- Computer-assisted coding with concurrent automated record review
- CDI 3D case-finding as documentation is entered
- Mobile app for real-time provider query responses
- Cloud SaaS or on-premises deployment options


**Best for:** Large hospitals seeking a mature, integrated CAC and CDI platform rather than full coding autonomy.


## How to Evaluate Autonomous Coding and CDI Together


Test whether an autonomous medical software identifies documentation gaps during coding, before claims reach billing.


When comparing platforms, confirm:


- **Alert vs. query logic:** Does it distinguish education-only gaps from issues that require the chart to be held?
- **One workflow or two products:** Are coding and CDI integrated or deployed as separate modules?
- **Who writes the query:** Does the platform generate a compliant provider query, or does a human specialist write it?
- **Explainability per medical code:** Can you trace each code to its supporting documentation, applied rule, and rationale?
- **Connection to claim outcomes:** Does the platform use denial and reimbursement data to propose improvements, or does it stop at coding?


> By these criteria, CombineHealth is built to pass all five: coding and CDI run in one workflow, not two products; it generates compliant provider queries rather than only flagging gaps; it distinguishes CDI alerts from queries; every code is traceable to its documentation, applied rule, and rationale; and it connects to claim outcomes, using denials, reimbursements, and underpayments to propose validated improvements.
>
>
> That integration is why, in a 400-bed hospital deployment, it surfaced 5× more CDI opportunities than the manual workflow — documentation gaps a coding-only tool would pass straight to billing.


## Why Combining Autonomous Coding and CDI Matters


**An accurate medical code based on incomplete documentation can still lead to a**[denial](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/denial-management-in-healthcare) **.** When coding and CDI operate in separate products, documentation gaps can go undetected until they reach billing.


This creates rework. A chart may contain a technically valid medical code that lacks supporting documentation, giving the payer grounds to challenge it after billing and adjudication. By then, resolving the issue may require resubmission, an[appeal](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/how-to-appeal-an-insurance-claim-denial) , or a write-off instead of a provider query raised during coding.


Many autonomous medical coding vendors offer CDI as an add-on or flag documentation gaps for separate review. CombineHealth integrates documentation review into the[autonomous medical coding](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/autonomous-medical-coding-guide) workflow, **helping identify gaps before claims reach billing.**


> **Recommended read:**[Adjudication Process in Healthcare](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/claims-adjudication-process-in-healthcare)

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How does CombineHealth combine autonomous coding and CDI in one workflow?


CombineHealth evaluates documentation sufficiency in the same pass as coding. As it assigns ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS, E/M, and modifier codes, it flags missing specificity, unsupported diagnoses, contradictory documentation, missing critical-care time, and medical-necessity gaps — then either finalizes a supported encounter or raises a CDI alert or query. There's no separate CDI product or second queue.


### Does CombineHealth generate provider queries, or only flag documentation gaps?


It generates them. CombineHealth distinguishes CDI alerts (lower-risk gaps tracked for provider education) from CDI queries (clarification needed before coding is finalized), and generates and routes compliant provider queries automatically — rather than only flagging a gap for a human specialist to write up later.


### How many more CDI opportunities does CombineHealth surface?


In a 400-bed hospital deployment, CombineHealth identified 5× more CDI opportunities than the manual workflow — because it reviews the complete encounter for documentation gaps while it codes, catching missing specificity, unsupported diagnoses, and medical-necessity gaps that a coding-only pass would send straight to billing.


### Can CombineHealth audit codes our EHR or coders already produced for documentation gaps?


Yes. CombineHealth runs in an audit mode that reviews codes assigned by providers, EHRs, or existing coding teams against the clinical documentation, flagging unsupported selections, missed coding opportunities, and documentation gaps, so you can add AI-powered coding and CDI review alongside your current process without replacing it.


### What is the difference between a CDI alert and a CDI query?


A CDI alert flags a gap for provider education without stopping coding; a CDI query holds the chart and asks the provider directly before coding finalizes. Platforms that only alert can miss charts where a medical code can't be finalized without an answer.


### Can autonomous coding really catch documentation gaps without a human reviewing every chart?


Yes, when CDI logic runs inside the same pass as coding, flagging gaps as codes are assigned, not after the fact. Routine charts go untouched by humans; charts with genuine gaps are held for review. Automation rates vary by vendor, so test on your own charts.


### Does integrated CDI actually reduce coding-related denials?


Yes, it catches the documentation issue before the claim is submitted instead of after a payer rejects it.


### What should HIM and CDI leaders ask a vendor before signing?


Ask whether coding and CDI run as one workflow or two products, whether it generates compliant queries itself or just flags issues, and whether every decision carries a per-medical-code audit trail. Then test it on your own encounters.
